result: At pinned modelcontextprotocol/rust-sdk commit 4a738b9dd99eaca418b614afa433a0cbdaf8d056, crates/rmcp/src/service/server.rs gives source-level evidence for server-side initialize retention. The normal initialize path matches ClientRequest::InitializeRequest, clones initialize_request.params into negotiated_peer_info, constructs Peer::new(..., Some(negotiated_peer_info.clone())), and passes a RequestContext containing peer.clone() into service.handle_request for the initialize call. After InitializeResult, it changes only negotiated_peer_info.protocol_version to the negotiated response version and stores the object with peer.set_peer_info before entering serve_inner; the source comment states that subsequent request handlers then observe the negotiated protocol version through context.protocol_version(). Combined only with own worker205/earlier own-role capability test context, this replaces the remaining server-side propagation inference with source-backed full-params peer/request-context retention. It does not prove ordinary handler access to every capability field, deployed ChatGPT connector behavior, transport availability, process-loss durability, or richer-mode parity.
